description: Optimal hash table solution with proactive edge case analysis and clear Big-O reasoning.

transcript.text: Welcome! Today we will solve the Two Sum problem.
Thank you! Before coding, let me clarify: can there be negative numbers? Can the same element be used twice? And is there always exactly one valid pair?
Yes, numbers can be negative. You cannot use the same element twice. There is guaranteed to be one unique answer.

Great. A brute force approach checks all pairs in O(n^2) time and O(1) space. We can optimize this using a hash map to achieve O(n) time and O(n) space. As we iterate through the list, for each number x, we look up target - x in the map. If present, we return [map[target - x], current_index]. Otherwise, we store x and its index.
Sounds optimal! Go ahead and write the solution.
I have written the solution. I also accounted for duplicate values by checking complement before inserting.
What are the time and space complexities?
Time complexity is O(n) on average because dictionary lookup and insertion are O(1) average time. Space complexity is O(n) in the worst case where we store up to n elements in the dictionary.
